l4_law_assessment.law: L4 PROVENANCE (GOAL.md, binding): Every training token carries a receipted lineage (source → generator → verifier chain, all local). Data auditability is constitutional.
l4_law_assessment.finding: The checkpoint step-00000766 exists, has integrity (hash verified), and demonstrates trainedness (2× baseline performance on in-distribution eval). However, the ORIGINAL TRAINING RUN has no discoverable receipt linking its input data source to this checkpoint output. The checkpoint manifests its own hash but does not name the corpus it trained on. No training receipt exists in accessible records.
l4_law_assessment.conclusion: L4 PROVENANCE VIOLATION CONFIRMED — the checkpoint's training data source is not recoverable from local records. The violation is CLOSURE-BLOCKING: C-BASE cannot proceed to in-distribution verification without knowing what distribution it trained on.

recommendation: Path B (re-run with provenance) is the lowest-risk cure. The checkpoint shows trainedness but its provenance is lost. A re-run produces a new checkpoint with full documentation, satisfies L4, and is gated by the same budget-approved training harness. Path A (locate missing receipt) is archaeology with uncertain recovery time. Path C (waive L4) sets a precedent for provenance gaps.
next_action: Awaiting team-lead ruling on cure path.
notes: Post-hoc eval demonstrates trainedness convincingly (2× baseline is not random-init performance). However, evaluation IS NOT provenance. The eval named the data distribution (c14-increment-mod-8 corpus-v2) but that is WHICH TASK the checkpoint learned, not WHERE IT TRAINED. The fact that the checkpoint learned task-specific behavior proves it trained on SOME corpus, but leaves L4 violated (the source corpus, its generation receipts, and the training-to-checkpoint link are all unknown).
